questions.q: What distinguishes a positional argument from an optional argument in argparse?
options: Positional arguments always take default values; optional ones never do
A positional argument is required and identified by its position; an optional argument is identified by a flag like --threshold
Optional arguments must come before positional ones
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: Positional arguments are required and matched by their order on the command line. Optional arguments are matched by their flag name and commonly have a default value.

questions.q: How do you define a flag (an argument that takes no value, like --verbose) in argparse?
options: parser.add_argument("--verbose", type=bool)
parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
parser.add_argument("--verbose", default=True)
parser.add_argument("--verbose", required=True)
questions.explain: action="store_true" makes the argument a flag: its value becomes True if the flag was passed on the command line, and False otherwise, with no value needed after it.

questions.q: Where does argparse's --help output come from?
options: You must write it manually as a separate string
It's generated automatically from the descriptions passed to ArgumentParser and add_argument
It is fetched from the Python documentation at runtime
argparse does not support a --help option
questions.explain: argparse builds the --help screen automatically from the description and help text you supply when defining the parser and its arguments.

questions.q: By convention, what does an exit code of 0 communicate when a script calls sys.exit(0)?
options: The script crashed
The script succeeded
The script is still running
The script requires elevated permissions
questions.explain: An exit code of 0 is the universal convention for success; any nonzero exit code signals some kind of failure or specific condition.

questions.q: If --threshold is defined with `default=90`, what happens if a user runs the script without passing --threshold at all?
options: argparse raises an error because the argument is missing
args.threshold is set to 90 automatically
args.threshold is set to None
The script fails to parse any arguments
questions.explain: When an optional argument has a default value and the user doesn't supply it, argparse fills in that default automatically — no error is raised.
